summary.title: Paper in 3 Minutes
keyPoints: Ten actionable rules provide a systematic approach to safe rTAPP surgery
Rules are organized by surgical phase: entry, dissection, mesh placement, fixation, closure
Each rule addresses a specific failure mode or danger point
Mnemonic-based learning facilitates recall during surgery
Adherence to all 10 rules significantly reduces complications
summary.clinicalPearl: These rules are not guidelines - they are binary requirements. Violating any single rule puts the patient at risk.

activities.title: Rule Recall Challenge
activities.instruction: Match each surgical scenario to the Golden Rule it violates

matchItems.scenario: Mesh fixation placed below the iliopubic tract laterally
matchItems.explanation: Fixation below the iliopubic tract risks nerve entrapment in the Triangle of Pain

matchItems.scenario: Beginning medial dissection before identifying the IEV
matchItems.explanation: The IEV is the primary orientation landmark and must be identified before any dissection

matchItems.scenario: Proceeding with mesh when only 3 quadrants are visible
matchItems.explanation: All four quadrants must be visualized before mesh placement

flashcards.front: Rule 1: What landmark must be identified first?
flashcards.back: The inferior epigastric vessels (IEV). They are your anatomical compass for the entire procedure.

flashcards.front: Rule 2: What must be done before any peritoneal incision?
flashcards.back: Identify the boundaries of your dissection and ensure you are in the correct plane.

flashcards.front: Rule 3: Where should you NOT dissect blindly?
flashcards.back: Into the Triangle of Doom or Triangle of Pain. Never dissect into areas where you cannot clearly identify structures.
Complete separation of vas deferens and spermatic vessels from peritoneum with visualization of the inverted-Y.

flashcards.front: Rule 5: What must be achieved before placing mesh?
flashcards.back: The Critical View of the Myopectineal Orifice (CV-MPO) - all four quadrants visualized.

flashcards.front: Rule 6: What are the minimum mesh overlap requirements?
flashcards.back: Adequate coverage of all potential hernia sites with appropriate overlap beyond defect margins.

flashcards.front: Rule 7: Where must you avoid fixation?
flashcards.back: Below the iliopubic tract laterally (Triangle of Pain) and in the Triangle of Doom. Only Zone 2 is safe for fixation.

flashcards.front: Rule 8: How should peritoneum be closed?
flashcards.back: Complete closure to prevent mesh contact with bowel and reduce risk of adhesive small bowel obstruction.
Photographs of the CV-MPO achieved, mesh position, and peritoneal closure for quality assurance.

flashcards.front: Rule 10: When should you convert to open?
flashcards.back: When landmarks cannot be identified, planes are not developing, or patient safety requires it.

questions.question: Which landmark must be identified before starting any dissection?
questions.explanation: Rule 1: IEV must be identified first as the primary orientation landmark.

questions.question: What must be achieved before mesh placement?
questions.explanation: Rule 5: CV-MPO must be achieved before placing mesh.

questions.question: Which zone is safe for mesh fixation?
questions.explanation: Rule 7: Only Zone 2 (medial, above Cooper's) is safe for fixation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Rule 10?
questions.explanation: Rule 10 establishes when conversion to open surgery is appropriate for safety.

questions.question: Why must peritoneum be closed completely (Rule 8)?
questions.explanation: Complete peritoneal closure prevents mesh contact with bowel and adhesive SBO.

takeaways: The 10 Golden Rules are binary requirements, not optional guidelines
Each rule prevents a specific complication or failure mode
Know all 10 rules by heart before operating independently
pitfalls: Treating the rules as guidelines rather than requirements
Not documenting adherence to each rule
